scholarships.title: Walczak NAWA Programme
scholarships.degree: Doctoral (PhD students and doctoral-school participants); also doctors and academic teachers
scholarships.official_source: Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA)

existing.description: The Walczak NAWA Programme funds international mobility for researchers in medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences connected with Polish institutions, letting them carry out research and work alongside leading specialists in the best medical centres worldwide. Participants choose a teaching, research or clinical track for a stay of one to six months. Eligible applicants are PhD students and doctoral-school participants, doctors with at least a doctorate working in hospitals and other medical institutions, and academic teachers in the medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences. The support, described by NAWA as covering a stipend, living and accommodation costs and travel expenses, amounts to up to PLN 32,000 for each month of stay, with a one-off PLN 20,000 for doctoral students and researchers on the scientific path whose stay exceeds three months. NAWA's call page still shows the December 2024 edition as the most recent announcement.
eligibility: PhD students and participants in doctoral schools
Doctors with at least a doctorate working in hospitals and other medical institutions
Academic teachers at universities and research units in the medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to PhD students and participants in doctoral schools, doctors holding at least a doctorate who work in hospitals and other medical institutions, and academic teachers at universities and research units in the medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences. Participants develop their competencies in one of three tracks - teaching, research or clinical - during a stay of one to six months abroad.
benefits: Up to PLN 32,000 for each month of stay
Stipend plus living and accommodation costs
One-off PLN 20,000 for scientific-path stays longer than three months
coverage: Up to PLN 32,000 for each month of stay in a foreign host centre
One-off material support of PLN 20,000 for doctoral students and researchers on the scientific path staying longer than three months
application_method: Submit through the NAWA ICT system, which the programme page names as the submission channel
Applications require a host institution invitation, a promoter's opinion and a supervisor opinion per the published appendices
existing.notes: The programme was commissioned by the Minister of Health under the 2018 biomedical cooperation agreement signed in Washington and developed with substantive support from the Medical Research Agency, which enabled it to open beyond the United States. NAWA still lists it among its active programmes for scientists, and three editions have awarded 57 grants totalling PLN 4,299,000 for stays in US medical centres.
existing.duration: A stay of between one and six months in a foreign host centre, in one of three tracks: teaching, research or clinical
existing.application_period: Annual editions (2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024); no new edition has been announced since the December 2024 call
existing.deadline_display: The most recent published announcement is no. 41/2024 of 5 December 2024 for the Walczak NAWA 2024 edition; the programme page still states that the call for applications runs until 31 January 2024 in the NAWA ICT system.
existing.program_type: Medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences research internship and professional development grant

existing.description: The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program is a nine-month non-degree professional development scholarship for graduates from Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan who already have at least two years of professional experience. Grantees attend two semesters of classes at one of about fifteen affiliated Polish universities, take part in an introductory course, trainings and grantees' conventions, and complete at least two weeks of professional internship. The programme provides support valued at PLN 6,000 per month, free access to university classes, accommodation, health insurance and a return ticket to Poland. It was founded by the Polish-American Freedom Foundation and is financially supported by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA).
eligibility: Citizenship and permanent residence in Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan
Age under 40 (under 45 for the Kirkland Research track)
At least two years of professional experience
At least a two-year break from any previous scholarship abroad lasting more than six months
Studies can be conducted in Polish or English; English-medium study is not available to candidates from Belarus and Ukraine
Polish at B2 required to start, B1 minimum at interview; candidates studying in English need English at B2 and Polish at A1
Not eligible: holders of a Polish residence card, and people living or working in Poland when applying
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens and permanent residents of Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan (plus Tajikistan and Uzbekistan for the research track) who hold a completed 5-year higher education degree, are under 40 (45 for the research track), have at least two years of professional experience, and have not held a comparable scholarship abroad in the previous two years. Holders of a Polish residence card and people living or working in Poland at the time of application are ineligible.
benefits: Free access to university classes and academic advising
Accommodation for the entire stay in Poland
Health insurance covering outpatient care, emergency treatment and civil liability
One return ticket to Poland up to an agreed amount
Public transport cards, visa costs and research materials
Introductory course, three or four grantees' conventions, personal development trainings and a two-semester Polish language course
coverage: PLN 6,000 per month of support (programme site, current edition)
Free access to university classes and academic advisor support
Accommodation for the whole stay in Poland
Health insurance (outpatient care, emergency treatment, civil liability)
One return ticket to Poland up to an agreed amount
Public transport cards and visa costs
Research materials, introductory course, grantees' conventions and Polish language course
requirements: Candidates must intend to return to their home country after the scholarship and implement the project prepared under it
Must specify a study offer in the chosen language at one of the participating Polish academic centres
Application instructions are published by the Programme Office on kirkland.edu.pl
documents: Completed online application via the Kirkland programme system
Proof of citizenship and permanent residence in an eligible country
Proof of completed 5-year higher education degree
Documentation of at least two years of professional experience
Project/study plan for the scholarship period
Language certificates evidencing Polish and/or English levels
Recommendation letters as required by the current edition's rules
existing.english_requirement: English B2 for candidates from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Moldova, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan who plan to study in English; Polish B2 to start and B1 minimum at interview for those studying in Polish. Study in English is not possible for candidates from Belarus and Ukraine.
application_method: Online application through the Kirkland programme system described at kirkland.edu.pl/dla-kandydatow/
Applications can also be requested by e-mail from the Programme Office
existing.selection_notes: The documented process is staged: eligibility review, review of proposed study projects by independent experts, then interviews. Stated preferences are candidates actively working in their professional and social fields, candidates with significant achievements, candidates who have not studied in Poland before, and candidates choosing studies in Polish.
existing.best_fit: Graduates from Eastern Europe, the South Caucasus and Central Asia with at least two years of professional experience pursuing a nine-month professional development stay in Poland.
existing.notes: The Kirkland Research Program runs in parallel as a one-semester research stay for PhD holders with an established academic position, paid at PLN 2,200 per month for four months with accommodation, travel reimbursement, a scientific/didactic package up to PLN 3,500 and insurance. The parallel Kirkland Research scholarship is a different award and should not be merged into this row.
existing.duration: Nine months (two semesters) of university classes plus at least two weeks of professional internship, introductory course and grantees' conventions; a parallel Kirkland Research track runs four months
existing.application_period: Annual cycle; the 2026/27 scholarship year was inaugurated in September/October 2026, so applications for the next edition are expected before that
existing.deadline_display: No application deadline is published for the 2027/28 edition as of 2026-10-04. The programme runs on an annual cycle: kirkland.edu.pl reports 'Uroczyste zakończenie XXVI edycji Programu Kirklanda' (graduation of the 26th edition) and 'Inauguracja roku stypendialnego 2026/27' in September/October 2026, and the recruitment calendar is published on the Polish candidates page.
existing.program_type: Non-degree professional development scholarship with internship
